equipment.provDetail.stronge_realistic: Cushion friction curve fitted on reference slow-motion footage; omega_ratio = 1.8 adopted from the reference resolver's default (the kick anchors are all gross-slip and cannot calibrate it).
equipment.provDetail.pool_used: Ball–ball friction for worn or dirty balls, fitted jointly on reference slow-motion footage (topspin hop apex 1.1–3.1 mm, two solved-camera cut throws, a stun null; loss 0.49 vs 4.40 for the Marlow fit). Published dirty-ball throw measurements support the raised friction floor.
equipment.provDetail.aramith_pool_worn: Ball–ball friction for worn or dirty balls, fitted jointly on reference slow-motion footage (topspin hop apex 1.1–3.1 mm, two solved-camera cut throws, a stun null; loss 0.49 vs 4.40 for the Marlow fit). Published dirty-ball throw measurements support the raised friction floor.
equipment.provDetail.wpa_generic_9ft: Legacy compatibility geometry, not a WPA reference despite its id: the original default table's pocket layout, measured from a 7-ft home table, on the WPA 9-ft surface with the WPA nose height. Its pocket mouths (5.07 in and 5.94 in) and facing angles fall outside the WPA bands. It stays so that old replays and links open on the table they were recorded on.
equipment.provDetail.pool_worsted_new: Dr. Dave physical-properties FAQ u_s = 0.2; Waldron stimpmeter u_r; the reference simulator's default spin decay, identical to the kernel default.
equipment.provDetail.simonis_860_tournam: Dr. Dave physical-properties FAQ u_s = 0.2; Waldron stimpmeter u_r; the reference simulator's default spin decay, identical to the kernel default.
equipment.provDetail.carom_worsted_heate: The reference simulator's generic carom friction trio: u_s 0.2, u_r 0.01 and the radius-proportional spin-decay default (the pool cloths' convention, paired with the carom balls' f_c = 0.15). Its source calls these values not well researched, and no better citable carom-cloth measurement was found. Named residual: UMB rules require a heated slate (about 5 °C above ambient), and no citable friction model of that heating exists; heated worsted is faster than pool cloth in every source.
equipment.provDetail.pool_standard: Dr. Dave physical-properties FAQ and the generic pool ball parameters (m = 0.170097 kg, R = 28.575 mm): the kernel default parameter set.
equipment.provDetail.aramith_pool: Dr. Dave physical-properties FAQ and the generic pool ball parameters (m = 0.170097 kg, R = 28.575 mm): the kernel default parameter set.
equipment.provDetail.carom: Generic carom ball parameters (m = 0.210 kg, R = 30.75 mm, f_c = 0.15): mass and diameter match the UMB norm; friction and restitution are estimates that their source calls not well researched.
equipment.provDetail.snooker_ash: Mixed-tier record. Mass 0.49 kg (17.3 oz), literature band: snooker cues run 16–18.5 oz, and the reference simulator's generic snooker cue (0.478 kg) sits in the same band. Tip radius 8.95 mm, estimated: no snooker crown radius is published, and a 9.5 mm tip is conventionally dressed to the tighter dime curvature, a convention rather than a measurement. End mass 6.67 g, estimated: the generic snooker cue's 4.67 g (ball mass / 30) plus about 2.0 g for the brass ferrule. Tip restitution 0.73 (literature); shaft first mode 28 Hz, estimated near the 27 Hz maple anchor.

help.title: How to play
help.pointerNote: Mouse and trackpad share the same controls — the game can't tell which one you're using, so both are shown.
help.controls.mouse.aim.v: Aim — the cue swings to your pointer (a small dead zone around the cue ball prevents accidental snaps)
help.controls.mouse.hand.k: Left-drag from the cue ball (ball in hand)
help.controls.mouse.hand.v: Move the cue ball to a legal spot
help.controls.mouse.orbit.v: Orbit the camera (Shift + left-drag also orbits when you're not aiming)
help.controls.mouse.pan.v: Pan the view across the table (stays within the table bounds)
help.controls.mouse.wheelZoom.v: Zoom — the plain wheel also zooms when you're not aiming
help.controls.mouse.aimView.v: Aiming follows your drag instead of snapping to the pointer; drag the right button up or down to pull the stroke back and set power
help.controls.mouse.call.k: Click a pocket marker or a highlighted ball
help.controls.mouse.call.v: Call the pocket or nominate the ball when the game asks for a call
help.controls.trackpad.aim.v: Aim — same as the mouse left-drag
help.controls.trackpad.scrollPower.v: Set shot power — scrolling is power, not zoom, while you aim
help.controls.trackpad.scrollZoom.v: Zoom — plain scrolling also zooms when you're not aiming
help.controls.trackpad.aimView.v: Same as the mouse: drag-relative aim; a secondary-click drag up or down sets power
help.controls.keyboard.power.v: Nudge power by 0.1 m/s (0.5 m/s with Shift)
help.controls.keyboard.spin.v: Tab to the pad under Elevation, then move the cue tip 0.01 R per press (0.1 R with Shift); Home centres it
help.controls.keyboard.seek.v: Seek the replay by 1 s (5 s with Shift)
help.controls.keyboard.seekEnds.v: Jump to the start / end of the replay
help.controls.touch.aim.v: Aim — slow drags automatically switch to fine aiming (down to 0.1×)
help.controls.touch.place.k: Drag from the cue ball (ball in hand)
help.controls.touch.place.v: Place the cue ball — a ghost ring floats above your finger
help.controls.touch.zoom.v: Zoom (a two-finger gesture in aim view exits it in place first)
help.controls.touch.pan.v: Pan the view across the table
help.controls.touch.call.k: Tap a pocket marker or a highlighted ball
help.controls.touch.call.v: Call the pocket or nominate the ball; a pocket list is also available
help.controls.touch.fire.v: Shoot — the shot only ever fires from this button
help.controls.touch.power.v: Set shot power — slide away from the gauge for fine control
help.controls.touch.spin.v: Open the spin and elevation sheet
help.controls.touch.fine.v: Fine-aim in 0.05° steps, repeating while held
help.flow.aim.d: Drag on the table (or press ← / →) until the cue points where you want.
help.flow.spin.d: Drag the dot on the cue-ball pad (or focus the pad and use the arrow keys) to set side, top or back spin; raise the cue with the elevation control for jump and massé shots.
help.flow.power.d: Scroll while aiming, press ↑ / ↓, or use the power slider.
help.flow.shoot.d: Press Shoot — or the FIRE button on touch.
help.flow.replay.d: Replay the shot and toggle slow motion from the playback controls.
help.flow.share.d: Share copies a replay link; the same shot plays back identically for anyone who opens it.
help.flow.playback.d: Playback records every session by itself — open it to browse your games, scrub the timeline and save a clip to Photos or Files.
help.games.nine_ball: Hit the lowest-numbered ball first; pocket the 9 on any legal shot to win.
help.games.eight_ball: Pocket your whole group — solids or stripes — then the 8 to win; the 8 is only legal last.
help.games.snooker: Alternate reds and colours (colours re-spot while reds remain); highest score wins.
help.games.carom_3cushion: No pockets: score by driving the cue ball off both other balls with at least three cushions before the second — every ball on the table is “legal”.
help.games.one_pocket: You score only in your single assigned corner pocket; any ball is legal — first to eight balls in your pocket wins.

drills.desc.bu-f1: Pot the 1 into the corner at rising cut angles. Ladder scoring over 10 shots.
drills.desc.bu-f2: Straight pot — the cue ball must stop dead on the ghost spot. Distance climbs.
drills.desc.bu-f3: Straight pot — follow the cue ball onto the paper target ahead.
drills.desc.bu-f4: Straight pot — draw the cue ball back onto the paper target.
drills.desc.bu-f5: Stun shot — pot the side pocket and drift the cue ball down the table onto the paper target. Far positions rebound off the end rail.
drills.desc.bu-f6: Ten classic pots, one try each. One point per pocketed ball.
drills.desc.bu-f7: Same pot every time — send the cue ball to a new rail target each shot.
drills.desc.circle: Fifteen balls on a circle. Pot them all — the cue ball may never leave the circle.
drills.desc.l-drill: Six balls on an L near the corner. Run them without the cue ball touching a rail.
drills.desc.lineup: Fifteen balls at half-diamond gaps down the long string. Clear them in order from the foot end — cue ball in hand to start.
drills.desc.lineup-e2m: The half-diamond line cleared from both ends alternately, converging on the middle ball.
drills.desc.lineup-m2e: Start on the middle ball and clear outward, alternating toward both ends.
drills.desc.lineup-random: The fifteen slots are shuffled — clear the line by ball number wherever each ball landed.
drills.desc.lineup-lateral: Fifteen balls in a tight row across the table below the side pockets. Clear it end to end in order.
drills.desc.lineup-lat-e2m: The lateral row cleared from both ends alternately, converging on the middle ball.
drills.desc.lineup-lat-m2e: Start on the middle ball of the lateral row and clear outward, alternating toward both ends.
drills.desc.lineup-l: Fifteen balls in an L wrapping one corner pocket's quadrant. Clear it end to end — only that pocket counts.
drills.desc.lineup-l-e2m: The same L cleared from both leg ends alternately, converging on the corner ball — only the enclosed pocket counts.
drills.desc.lineup-diagonal: Fifteen balls on the diagonal. Clear them in order — any pocket counts.
drills.desc.ghost9: Ten racks against the ghost: break, take ball in hand, then run out. Any miss or foul loses the rack.
drills.desc.colours-clear: Pot the six colours from their spots in order — yellow to black. A miss or foul ends the run.
drills.desc.colours-line: Six colours lined across the table. Pot them left to right — a miss or foul ends the run.
drills.desc.lineup-called: Run the fifteen-ball line-up calling every pocket. A dry, scratched or wrong-pocket shot ends the run — so does crashing into another ball.
drills.desc.progressive-lineup: Run N balls in rotation. Clear them all and the next rack adds one; a miss drops one.
drills.desc.ghost10: Ten racks of 10-ball rotation against the ghost: ball in hand after every break. A scratch costs two; a miss ends the rack.
drills.desc.rotation15: Run seeded 15-ball rotation racks. Every foul adds a penalty — the lower your total, the better.
drills.desc.mighty-x: A dead-straight long pot where the cue must replace the object ball. The target tightens each rung.
drills.desc.century: 14.1 continuous — call every ball and keep the run alive. A miss or foul ends it; reach 100 for a century.
help.games.straight_pool: Call every shot and score one point per ball — when fourteen are down the rack rebuilds and your run keeps going; first to the target wins.

equipment.desc.standard: The house baseline: Dr. Dave's endmass squirt model at the kernel defaults — every other cue is measured against this one.
equipment.desc.low_deflection: Shepard's lowest-squirt endmass regime — the classic low-deflection build.
equipment.desc.break_phenolic: A break cue in the highest measured squirt band, with a hard phenolic tip for speed.
equipment.desc.standard_dime_tip: The baseline cue with a dime-radius tip — identical everywhere else.
equipment.desc.masse_trick: A massé cue whose contact envelope was measured frame-by-frame from real trick-shot footage.
equipment.desc.masse_trick_dwell: The massé cue refit with the finite-dwell tip model — the footage-fitted successor entry.
equipment.desc.carbon_ld: A carbon-fiber shaft at the lightest published endmass — the ultra-low-deflection regime.
equipment.desc.jump_phenolic: A short, light jump cue with a phenolic tip — built to hop the cue ball legally.
equipment.desc.snooker_ash: A snooker-pattern cue: lighter build, smaller tip convention, softer first mode.
equipment.desc.carom_conical: A three-cushion carom cue: heavier band floor, stiff conical response.
equipment.desc.pro_ld_pivot_141: Pro low-deflection shaft at the 2008 robot test's longest published pivot, 14.1 in — its lowest measured squirt.
equipment.desc.pro_ld_pivot_118: Pro low-deflection shaft at a published 11.8 in pivot from the 2008 robot test.
equipment.desc.pro_ld_pivot_101: Pro low-deflection shaft at a published 10.1 in pivot — matching Shepard's anchor point.
